evidence.claim: ~60% global harmonic (strain wave) reducer market share; harmonic reducers are the dominant joint transmission in humanoid robots requiring zero-backlash, high-ratio torque multiplication in compact form — 15-25 units per humanoid robot
evidence.source: Industry analysis; Harmonic Drive Systems investor materials; multiple robotics supply chain reports

evidence.claim: Lead times extended to 20-30 weeks for harmonic reducers as of late 2024; company guided for capacity expansion driven by humanoid robot demand in 2024-2025 earnings commentary
evidence.source: Harmonic Drive Systems earnings calls 2024-2025; supply chain channel checks

evidence.claim: Manufacturing barrier: flex spline (thin-walled steel cup flexing cyclically under load) requires metallurgy and heat treatment at sub-micron tolerances; 10-15 year learning curve; Chinese alternatives (Leaderdrive) are 20-40% less precise with shorter fatigue life
evidence.source: Technical analysis; industry comparison reports; Chinese domestic reducer qualification data

evidence.claim: Stock tripled 2022-2024 on humanoid demand expectations; Harmonic Drive Systems is the single most-cited supply chain bottleneck in humanoid robot BOM analysis across Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Citi robotics reports
evidence.source: Market data; Morgan Stanley Humanoid 100 report; Goldman Sachs humanoid supply chain analysis

evidence.claim: Cost per robot: $4,000-$16,000 in harmonic reducers alone (at $200-$800/unit × 20-25 joints) = 15-30% of total robot BOM; no viable substitute achieves equivalent backlash/precision/compactness
evidence.source: BOM analysis; industry cost breakdowns; Tesla Optimus teardown estimates

what_could_weaken_view: Direct-drive architecture adoption: if humanoid OEMs shift to high-torque direct-drive motors (no reducer at each joint), Harmonic Drive's humanoid demand collapses — Tesla Optimus currently uses both but architecture is not settled

Chinese domestic substitution: Leaderdrive (688017.SH) closes the spec gap on fatigue life and precision by 2027 — Chinese humanoid OEMs (Unitree, UBTech, AgiBot) source domestically, removing the largest demand growth vector

Valuation already re-rated: stock tripled on humanoid expectations; if humanoid production ramps slower than expected (units stay in thousands not hundreds of thousands through 2027), the stock de-rates before fundamentals catch up

Industrial robot demand cyclicality: Harmonic Drive's base business (FANUC, Yaskawa automation) is subject to manufacturing capex cycles; a global manufacturing slowdown compresses the base even as humanoid demand grows

New transmission technology: cycloidal drives, cable-driven actuators, or quasi-direct-drive approaches achieving competitive performance at lower cost — HEBI Robotics and others working on cable-driven alternatives
